expectation: When either provider account metadata read fails, a usage refresh still reads that provider usage and retains its last known account. Codex and Claude usage changes reach the CLI and open Agents info section, and after both account reads recover another refresh updates both usage values and retains the correct accounts.

A standalone chat left in the store as a hidden board task is converted once into its own model: it keeps its ID so the existing conversation transcript stays attached, keeps its provider session, carries its in-flight turn state across with the status message and progress report that explain it, is removed from the board so it never lists or resolves as a task, and reopening the chat returns that same migrated chat rather than creating a second one.

Each standalone chat page is its own provider session: the first turn of a page starts a fresh session carrying the system prompt, which explains the page metadata header and tells the agent to run chat page read only for a page the message continues, plus a Playhouse page metadata header, never a User line, that names the current page by title and ID with a shortened excerpt of its latest exchange and lists recent pages newest first by title and ID only. Later turns on that page resume it without repeating the header, and a different page never shares it, so an earlier page's turns never reach a later page. An annotation that quotes an earlier page carries that whole page into the current turn, marked as a Playhouse page. A page whose latest answer is long sends only the start of that answer, and the agent loads the whole page itself with the real chat page read command. Rotating sessions still leaves every page's messages visible in the transcript.

The Chat button opens the standalone chat — its own model rather than a board task — in a sliding sidebar that never appears on the board, task commands cannot reach it by ID, and the bridge rejects any attempt to add a repository or worktree root to it. The GUI composer works without a configured repository parent and omits task status, repository controls, the Changes sidebar, and the no-repository-selected banner. Its CLI page close-turn signal keeps a continuing reply on the active page and starts a new titled page on a topic change, a completed turn's user and assistant messages persist onto the active page without leaking onto other pages, and pages are findable by search. Each page is also stored in a separate atomic JSON file in a discoverable archive directory; pages already present before file archiving are backfilled once, and each file tracks current metadata and messages. A turn that omits close-turn is tracked as missed, then a background low-effort Luna fallback rejects one malformed classification and retries, moves both messages to its correctly titled page, keeps page evaluation visually quiet while the primary answer remains usable, then updates the transcript separator with the title when classification completes; a following send waits for that decision, and preserves chronological order on a later append. An explicit page start during a pending fallback cancels its stale result, keeps the missed turn on its original page, and clears the warning. If all helper results are invalid, the pending decision remains durable, blocks the next provider send, and retries after the helper recovers; the UI keeps the unresolved state visually quiet and sends successfully once recovery completes. Earlier pages stay visible in the transcript after their page session rotates, and a board task conversation rejects a chat page as turn context. While a chat turn is held active, queuing a follow-up on the chat resolves the chat rather than a board task and the queued message can be removed, and selecting the provider the chat already uses returns the chat unchanged instead of failing. The chat's own turn state changes (In Progress, then Waiting Response) during a send, and it never renders as a card on the visible Kanban board in any state. A chat turn that ran close-turn gets no nudge, and a Codex chat turn that skipped it gets exactly one nudge through the shared recovery loop, asking for close-turn on its reply and never for a task outcome, because the chat has no board status; its developer instructions teach it that task language means Playhouse's own board and give it the Playhouse task CLI, and they never ask it to write the page title into its visible answer. Opening a board task while the chat sidebar is showing replaces it with that task's conversation view instead of showing both at once, and returning to the board reveals the chat sidebar again, with the chat's own model left untouched by the unrelated task. The visible chat panel opens at full board-content height, overlaps the logo header and narrow board sidebar, and hides the covered branding and sidebar controls from accessibility navigation while open; it raises the board's minimum width by the chat panel width, so the window grows to keep the shifted columns visible; it pushes the columns to the panel’s right edge; closing chat reveals the sidebar while the window keeps its grown width, and the columns center in the board, now wider than they are. Dragging the chat sidebar's right border resizes it, between a 320-point minimum and the larger of its default width and the screen width the board's minimum width leaves free, and reopening the sidebar, even after an app relaunch, keeps the dragged width. The border's grab strip extends only out over the board, never over the transcript's scroller along its inner side, so pressing and dragging just inside the border leaves the width unchanged; hovering the border shows the left-right resize cursor, and hovering just inside it does not. While the edge moves, the chat keeps the width it was last laid out at, clipped to the panel, and its transcript reflows to the panel's width when the drag ends.

When a standalone chat uses Claude, a missed page signal invokes the Haiku helper at low effort; a malformed result is rejected and retried, an unrelated later question and its assistant reply move to a new titled page, the UI keeps page evaluation visually quiet without blocking the primary answer, updates the transcript separator when classification completes, and holds a following send until the decision resolves, and appends the related follow-up in chronological order. The Claude-specific model and effort arguments are verified through the real CLI/XPC path. An explicit page start during a pending fallback cancels its stale result, keeps the missed turn on its original page, and clears the warning. If all helper results are invalid, the pending decision remains durable, blocks the next provider send, and retries after the helper recovers; the UI keeps the unresolved state visually quiet and sends successfully once recovery completes.

Clicking Stop during Codex reasoning immediately moves the task to Waiting Response and sends Codex's turn-scoped turn/interrupt request. The accepted interruption settles the send without changing the task to Blocked, and a fresh CLI/XPC read confirms the status persisted. A fresh `conversation runtime` read from the daemon reports the turn active and interruptible while it thinks, and interrupted but no longer active once the stop settles. The turn's activity section renders open for as long as the daemon reports the turn active, and folds once the stop settles with no final answer. The observed Codex message time survives interruption and reload. In the window Continue replaces Stop at once, before the provider acknowledges the interrupt.

Clicking Stop during Claude reasoning immediately moves the task to Waiting Response and sends Claude's session-scoped control interrupt. The accepted interruption settles the send without changing the task to Blocked, and a fresh CLI/XPC read confirms the status persisted. A fresh `conversation runtime` read from the daemon reports the turn active and interruptible while it thinks, and interrupted but no longer active once the stop settles. The turn's activity section renders open for as long as the daemon reports the turn active, and folds once the stop settles with no final answer. In the window Continue replaces Stop at once, before the provider acknowledges the interrupt.

If Codex rejects turn/interrupt while its turn is still active, Stop reports the provider failure and the task returns to In Progress; in the window Continue replaces Stop at once and gives way to Stop again when the provider refuses; releasing the fixture lets the original turn complete normally into Waiting Response.

If Claude rejects its session control interrupt while its turn is still active, Stop reports the provider failure and the task returns to In Progress; in the window Continue replaces Stop at once and gives way to Stop again when the provider refuses; releasing the fixture lets the original turn complete normally into Waiting Response.

Playhouse opens one main board window titled with its worktree label, displays the transparent theater logo in the board header, keeps a fixed standard-width (216-point) Kanban sidebar, 8% wider than its previous 200-point width and left of the columns while they scroll, and places its Scheduled Tasks button inside the sidebar below the full logo header. The board's columns start at its top, just below the header instead of centering in a board taller than they are; they center across a board wider than they are and start just right of the sidebar in a narrower one. The Dock AppIcon uses the same foreground artwork on a solid #2C2F36 background, and the bridge reports API version 1.

The primary and linked source worktrees resolve to stable, distinct app and XPC identities, build paths, data stores, logs, and managed worktree roots, each worktree root inside its data directory. The run.sh launch resolver replaces a PLAYHOUSE_DATA_DIRECTORY inherited from another Playhouse app's profile directory with the launching worktree's own and rejects any other foreign data directory, and run.sh drops PLAYHOUSE_BRIDGE_SERVICE_NAME and PLAYHOUSE_BRIDGE_SOCKET_PATH inherited from another Playhouse app, saying so, while keeping the launching worktree's own bridge. run.sh keeps this worktree's running app open during its build and stops this worktree's app and bridge daemon only once, after the build and right before it opens the app, so a daemon started from the previous build during the build cannot serve the new app. A saved conversation remains visible after an app restart.

New Task opens with the repository picker closed and composer focused; no selected repository is valid and shows no red missing-folder warning when the required repository root is configured. A standalone conversation can be sent without repository roots, while GUI and CLI reject sends if the configured repository root is missing. The UI and CLI accept standalone sends after the root is configured, and such a send runs its provider in the configured repository root rather than the home folder, with instructions saying so. The CLI accepts empty-root tasks and rejects blank titles, missing folders, unavailable roots, and invalid merge targets.

A Claude task with no repository or folder starts its session in the configured repository root, and a later turn resumes that native session, without handoff context, in the folder its session recorded even after the repository root setting changes; a side chat forks and continues that session in the same recorded folder. A new rootless task follows the changed root, and when a session's recorded folder no longer exists the resumed turn runs in the current repository root.

A directly created conversation can add repositories in order, edit pending branch settings, and add a context folder; these settings persist across fresh connections without creating branches or worktrees before the first send. The conversation shows the additional context folder without repeating repository worktrees in a Working in summary. Saving an unsent prompt records task creation, prompt save, and subsequent reads with safe argument metadata, result state, and outcome while excluding prompt text.
A selected existing branch remains pending until task start, then reuses its exact existing worktree path.

The conversation picker can add multiple repositories; unset branch settings display defaults and persist pending auto records resolved to local main without creating branches or worktrees before the first send.
A folder-only task persists its context without Git worktrees and reaches Done after a successful turn without attempting a merge.
Adding a repository branch already assigned to another active task is rejected in the new conversation, and the existing task and repository reservation remain unchanged.
Two concurrent CLI/XPC creates targeting the same explicit branch in one repository serialize through a shared cross-process lock, leaving exactly one persisted active task and rejecting the other.

If another process holds the shared task-store write lock when a Codex turn completes after an explicit completed outcome, final status persistence waits and then saves Review status and full history across fresh CLI/XPC reads. Correlated persistence diagnostics include task ID, store path, lock wait, attempts, and retry count; task reads correlate started and completed events by read ID and store path, while failed reads include store file and sidecar state. Reopening the conversation in the UI shows the saved exchange without a store error.

A real ModelContainer open failure against an isolated invalid store path returns an error and durably logs the phase, exact underlying NSError domain/code/userInfo, resolved store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and read-only schema probe failure; the paired visible UI case keeps Playhouse open on its normal board while the same isolated CLI/XPC request fails and verifies the persisted diagnostic.

A real SwiftData fetch failure against an isolated store with a missing task column returns an error and logs a correlated read ID, NSError domain/code/userInfo, store path, file/sidecar snapshot, and the exact missing-column message from a read-only schema probe before the CLI/XPC request completes; the paired visible UI case keeps the normal task board open and verifies the same isolated failure record.

A real legacy SwiftData task store with in-progress timing columns and no submitted-prompt column waits for the store-write lock while CLI/XPC reads concurrently; migration backs up before adding the missing VARCHAR prompt column as nullable with no default and preserves elapsed time at zero. The CLI preserves the task and its saved prompt, which a store from before drafts were flagged does not restore as a draft, and the visible app opens the migrated store with an empty composer that keeps the saved prompt through a subsequent restart with duration still zero; metadata advances and later opens create no additional backup. The store is imported once into the protected filename and the legacy database remains unchanged. Committed WAL-only saved prompt data survives import, and a subsequent edited draft survives restart without reimport.

A test-built Playhouse service rejects a data directory outside the temporary test area and a linked store inside it before creating or opening either store; the visible app remains on its isolated board and can still read its tasks.

Tasks with the same automatic branch choice remain pending without creating a worktree before conversation start. When one task has claimed the generated branch, a send from the other (through the CLI) succeeds with its own suffixed branch and a separate worktree, leaving both tasks started; the opt-in live provider integration sends both turns concurrently and confirms each task gets a distinct branch and worktree.

Sending the first message derives an auto branch from the generated task title, with a prompt fallback when title generation fails. Every linked PR must be merged before the task can move to Done. App focus checks each linked PR no more than once per 20 seconds; rapid focus changes are coalesced into one refresh after the cooldown. An unmerged PR keeps its link and suppresses the completion button. PR links and the green completion button have hit targets of at least 30×30 points. After all PRs merge, a later focus check replaces their links with a green completion button; clicking it waits for the task lock and then trusts that already-confirmed merge state, moving the task to Done immediately without re-querying GitHub even if merge status changed while the lock was held. The CLI's task move command has no such cached state, so it always verifies merge status directly with GitHub before completing, including rechecking after waiting for a contended task lock, and reports unmerged pull requests instead of completing when a PR is not actually merged. Completion removes managed worktrees while preserving their branches, does not merge into the local target, retains conversation history, and exposes the task in the searchable archive, whose conversation keeps its composer for follow-up questions; the CLI and the visible archive search the task's stored transcript, matching both the user's prompts and the assistant's replies case-insensitively; the visible archive loads the newest 40 first, and reveals older tasks as the user scrolls. While only some linked PRs are merged, each merged PR's number shows in merged purple and the task offers no completion checkmark until all are merged. The archive slides in from the board header's archive button as a 340-point SidePanel atom (done-archive-panel) along the window's trailing edge, and its close button slides it away until the button opens it again.

Two tasks with the same title and an automatic branch on one repository both start: the first gets the title slug, the second a fresh branch named like the slug plus a hyphen and four lowercase letters or digits, in a different worktree. An existing local branch named like the slug, with no task using it, is never checked out: a new automatic task gets a suffixed fresh branch started from its branch-from. The visible task conversation shows the resolved suffixed branch.

Moving a reviewed task to Done removes its managed worktree and keeps its branch and target commit without committing or merging. When the worktree holds uncommitted changes the move is refused until the user confirms discarding them: declining keeps the task in Review with its files intact, and confirming removes them. A reviewed task stays in Review until it is moved; in the UI the Done drawer rests as a thin sliver beside, not over, the board columns (once a board wider than its window is scrolled to its trailing end) and just left of the board scroller, which keeps the window edge, opens only while a reviewed card is dragged, and returns to rest both after a card is dropped on Done and when a card is dropped back in place without moving the task.

A Done task keeps its conversation open: the UI shows the composer with an archived hint saying a follow-up reopens the task in a fresh worktree from the merge target, instead of a read-only notice; its changes read reports no changes rather than a Git error for the removed worktree, and switching its provider is rejected. A follow-up sent from a Done task moves it back to In Progress before the turn starts, so it shows in the board's In Progress column while the agent works, with a fresh worktree renewed for the removed one. The real provider turn runs in that fresh worktree and is told it as an active task worktree rather than that the task is archived; its completed outcome moves the task to Review, the removed worktree stays removed, and the follow-up and its reply persist in the history across fresh reads. A Done task with no worktree to renew (one with only a context root) reopens to In Progress for its follow-up the same way, keeps that root, and its completed outcome moves it to Review.

A follow-up to a Done task whose merge target no longer exists cannot renew its removed worktree: the send fails with the missing merge target error, the task stays Done with no new worktree and no provider turn, and the follow-up is not left pending as a submitted prompt, so the UI composer keeps its text.

A Done task with only a context folder reopens without creating a worktree, but if that folder disappears and no default parent is configured, a bridge follow-up send fails before a provider turn starts; the task moves to Waiting Response, and the submitted prompt returns to its draft. The test then restores the folder so the UI can reopen the task and display the returned draft.

`task repository renew` starts follow-up Git work after a pull request merged. It is rejected while the repository has no linked pull request, while the linked pull request is unmerged, and while the merged worktree has uncommitted changes, leaving the task unchanged. A merged PR status read persists that it merged, and the next turn is told the merged branch is finished and to renew before Git changes. Renewing from inside the agent's turn retires the record with its merged PR to the task's past repositories, keeps the merged branch, removes the old worktree once that turn ends, and creates a fresh worktree on a new suffixed branch based on the merge target as just fetched from the remote, so it holds the merged commits even when the local target is stale. A new pull request then opens from the fresh worktree, and the card shows the merged PR in purple beside the new one; once the task is Done, the archive row lists both, and a pull request status read of the Done task, whose worktree was removed, lists only its recorded pull requests, the retired one marked past, without probing instead of failing. A Done task renews too: a follow-up to it returns it to In Progress before its turn starts, and `task repository renew` on a Done task does the same, each with a fresh worktree for every repository whose worktree was removed (a past link only for records that had a pull request); that turn's completed outcome moves it to Review, keeping both merged PRs on fresh reads.
The one-time lifecycle rollout clears task records and clean managed worktrees, preserves branches, and retains dirty managed worktrees with a notice.

With both pairs populated, the board keeps Blocked above Backlog and Waiting Response above In Progress, washes only the Waiting Response column in its purple tint (its pixels read purple where the other columns read neutral), allows vertical scrolling to reach lower backlog tasks, leaves Review as its own column, hides empty status sections, removes Done from the columns, and rejects manual changes to Codex-owned task status; ⌘F reveals and focuses a prominent board search that filters task cards by title as text changes, while close restores all cards. Answering a question without an explicit completed outcome leaves the task in Waiting Response. Task card titles use slightly expanded letter spacing and line spacing. The board's columns stay clickable where they draw after a sideways scroll followed by a new card, without needing a window resize. The board's scroller stays hidden until the pointer is over the board, then shows at a subdued opacity while the pointer rests there, and hides again once the pointer leaves; holding its knob makes it clearly more opaque than the same knob hovered, and releasing returns it to the subdued opacity. Each board column is built from plugin atoms: the empty In Progress and Review columns show their empty state while the populated Backlog does not, and the Backlog's Add button opens a new task conversation.

A task in Waiting Response moves to Review through the CLI and on the board, both from its card's Move to Review context-menu item, which Waiting Response and Blocked cards offer, and by dragging the card onto the Review column. The move runs the same review gate as a completed outcome: local changes on a PR-linked worktree are committed before the task reaches Review. It clears the waiting status, persists across a fresh CLI/XPC read, keeps the linked pull request, returns a task already in Review unchanged, and the moved task can still complete to Done. A Backlog task is rejected and keeps its status; a task whose turn is still running while it shows Waiting Response is rejected and keeps both its status and its uncommitted changes; and when the pull request sync fails, the move reports the error, shown on the board as an alert, and leaves the task in Waiting Response; once GitHub reports the pull request merged, a retry commits local work, skips syncing the merged branch even though its remote is unreachable, and moves the task to Review. Each transition into Waiting Response plays Ping and each transition into Review plays Glass; rejected and repeated moves play no sound.

A task in Waiting Response moves straight to Done, and a Blocked task moves to Review or straight to Done, through the CLI and on the board: Waiting Response and Blocked cards offer Move to Done in their context menu, Blocked cards also offer Move to Review, a Blocked card dragged onto the Review column lands in Review, and a Blocked card dragged onto the Done drawer lands in Done; a Backlog card offers neither and a Backlog task is still rejected for both moves and keeps its status. Moving a Waiting Response task to Done while its blocking question's turn still runs is rejected as still running, shown on the board in a Couldn't move task to Done alert, and keeps the task in Waiting Response with its worktree in place; once the turn finishes, Move to Done reaches Done and removes the task's clean Playhouse worktree as a move from Review does. Moving a Blocked task to Review clears its blocked reason and plays Glass; moving one to Done clears it too. Each move persists across a fresh CLI/XPC read, and a task already in Done is returned unchanged.

The CLI publishes standard and custom progress only during an active task turn, persists each report across fresh CLI/XPC connections, rejects invalid reports, and clears explicitly. During an active turn the CLI accepts completed and waiting-response outcomes, rejects invalid or inactive outcomes, and persists the selected status; provider processes started from the CLI/XPC service or the app's composer inherit that app's bridge service name and store directory, and an outcome reported with exactly that inherited environment reaches the task. A successful turn without an outcome and with nothing left running receives exactly one private recovery prompt that offers only the stopping outcomes; a completed report during it moves the task to Review, a waiting-response report during it leaves the task in Waiting Response, and no report by its end marks the task Blocked with the missing-outcome reason rather than Waiting Response, since the user was never asked anything. The board shows progress details and places completed tasks in Review and waiting outcomes in Waiting Response. New threads receive hidden progress and outcome instructions at thread start, and existing threads receive them on resume; turn requests do not repeat the instructions. Those instructions require updates at phase changes, around substantial tools, and at least every 30 seconds during long work; they offer no outcome for unfinished work and tell the agent to keep awaiting a required command within the turn. They place the outcome call, still the final CLI action, before the user-visible final reply, which ends the turn so it never ends on a tool call, and they tell the agent not to repeat an answer after a no-visible-output notice. Only an explicit completed outcome reaches Review. When a final answer ends with the outcome command written as text instead of run, the final answer, fresh history, and transcript hide that command, and it counts as the turn's outcome only when it names this task. A recovery prompt Playhouse sent shows its prompt and the agent's reply in history and the visible transcript, including after later ordinary turns. Fresh history after those prompts also retains the latest ordinary-turn diff while showing their replies. Completed and waiting-response outcomes start Glass and Ping respectively when their turns settle.

A turn has three stopping outcomes and none for unfinished work. A blocked report needs a reason and settles the task in Blocked with that reason; a blocked report without one, or with one longer than 500 characters, is rejected, as is a reason on any other outcome; a legacy in-progress report is answered with guidance, records nothing, withdraws an outcome staged earlier in the turn, and leaves the task In Progress. A turn that ends with no stopping outcome and nothing running gets exactly one private recovery prompt, during which the task stays In Progress; a completed report in that turn settles the task in Review, and a recovery turn that also ends unsettled leaves the task Blocked with a missing-outcome reason and no further prompts. The recovery prompt and its reply appear in the conversation history as a Playhouse-sent message and its reply. The user taking the work back ends Playhouse's private driving: stopping the recovery turn keeps the Stop's Waiting Response with no failure reason, and a queued follow-up runs next instead of a recovery prompt.

A Codex turn that ends without a stopping outcome while a required command it started is still running keeps the task In Progress, with no private prompt, for as long as the command runs, across many more reconciliations of the provider's background terminals than the old five-continuation allowance. When the command ends, Playhouse delivers its real exit status and output to Codex in exactly one private results turn, and the outcome Codex reports there settles the task: Review after a passing command; after a failing command either In Progress again while the agent's rerun is running and Review once the rerun passes, or Blocked with the agent's reason. A command that disappears without a result is reported to the agent as unknown, never as successful. A command still running when Playhouse's wait ceiling passes is reported as still running in the one results turn, is neither terminated nor waited for again, and a turn that ends unsettled after it leaves the task Blocked with the missing-outcome reason. Stopping the task while it waits terminates the command, leaves the task in Waiting Response with no failure reason, and starts no further turn. A turn that reports completed while leaving a command running, as with a dev server, settles in Review at once with no wait, no termination, and no results turn.

A follow-up the user queues while a task waits for a command its Codex turn left running ends the wait at once: the follow-up is the next turn the provider receives, ahead of any results or recovery prompt, and the command is neither terminated nor forgotten. When the follow-up's turn ends without a stopping outcome the task stays In Progress and Playhouse waits for the same command again, with no further prompt. When the command ends, its real exit status and output are delivered once in one private results turn, and the outcome Codex reports there settles the task in Review. The follow-up appears once in history.

A daemon killed while a task waits for a command its Codex turn left running does not strand the task: the next daemon finds the persisted wait, reconnects to the same app-server, keeps the task In Progress with no new prompt, and resumes reconciling the provider's background terminals. A command that ends after the restart has its real exit status and output delivered once, and the agent's rerun is waited for again. A command that ended while no daemon was connected is reported to the agent as having no result Playhouse saw, never as successful, and the agent's blocked outcome settles the task in Blocked with its reason. The user's message appears once in history across both restarts.

Progress reports clear when turns fail or are interrupted and when Codex requests user input; a staged completed outcome is discarded if its turn fails, leaving the task Blocked. The task card removes the report while lifecycle states remain Blocked or In Progress. A blocking structured question appears inline and moves the task to Waiting Response; its answer resumes the active turn in In Progress, and the answered turn finishes in Waiting Response. First-thread instructions distinguish source repository paths from active task worktree paths, allow read-only inspection without attaching a repo, and reserve repository add APIs for changes that need a worktree.
A rename waits for the real per-task operation lock, then persists across fresh CLI/XPC reads; rejecting a blank rename preserves the last valid title.

The conversation title has no copy button and its text is selectable: selecting and copying it places the task's exact persisted title on the pasteboard, including spaces, an ampersand and non-ASCII text, after a rename, and fresh CLI/XPC reads report the same title.

Root editing preserves order, removes duplicates, rejects an empty list, and waits for an active conversation turn; a stale Git-folder validation is rejected after a newer folder edit, and the newer roots remain saved.

Repository suggestions can be filtered and navigated with Up/Down, and Enter selects the highlighted repository; UI selection waits for an active turn and persists a pending auto branch. While the conversation is empty, a prominent theme-colored heading names all selected repositories and updates as repository APIs add or replace context; compact repository labels remain in the header without a duplicate repository summary. Dark and light themes use distinct prominent title colors, the supporting model prompt sits below with generous spacing, and the generic Start a conversation heading is absent. Additional context folders remain identifiable. The task repository API remains available during an active turn, prepares a managed worktree inside the app data directory's task-worktrees folder, updates saved repository selection, replaces repository context safely, and the paired UI shows API additions/removals. The main assistant is instructed to list repositories through Playhouse, inspect listed source paths read-only without attaching them, and add repositories only when it needs a task worktree for changes or commits.

Each repository row in the header's Add repository picker adds the repository alongside the selected ones when the row or its plus button is clicked, and its Replace button removes every selected repository and attaches only that one; the task repository API reaches the same add and replace results, adding an attached repository again gives it another worktree on its own branch, and the saved repository selection follows. The catalog's shared Overlay atom contains both actions and reveals them on hover; the UI keeps them visible over the row and buttons and hides them on exit. Both buttons sit clear of the list's overlay scroller and each shows a hover highlight while the pointer is on it.

Pending repository branch, merge-from, and merge-to settings wait for an active conversation turn, then persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads; invalid settings leave prior values intact, and settings are locked after worktree creation. Each setting is edited in place: the pencil beside a value opens an inline field with a checkmark that saves only that field and keeps the editor open on the saved value, and clicking outside the field or pressing Escape dismisses the edit without saving. The settings popover is wider than before with a larger title, and the repository chip's remove button is a larger target.

A branch-from that exists only on a Git remote and was never fetched is fetched when repository settings are saved, and the pending record stores its remote-tracking branch; a branch-from missing locally and on every remote is rejected without changing the saved settings; a remote that can't be reached reports the fetch failure instead of a missing branch and also keeps the saved settings; starting the task fetches the remote branch again, so its worktree starts from the remote's latest commit even after the remote branch moved ahead, without making the remote branch the task branch's upstream.

With no branch-from given, a repository without an origin remote keeps its local default branch, while a repository whose origin has the default branch stores origin's remote-tracking branch as the pending branch-from. Starting the task fetches origin first, so the worktree starts from origin's latest commit even when the local default branch and its remote-tracking ref are stale and the local branch holds unpushed commits, without making the remote branch the task branch's upstream. When origin can't be reached at start, the task still starts from the last fetched origin commit.
If a pending repository is removed while its settings are being validated, the stale edit is rejected and the newer repository removal and context root remain saved.

Removing one of two pending repositories leaves the remaining repository in task context and remembered settings, while preserving the removed source repository; the next task restores only the remaining remembered repository. Removing a pending repository preserves other context folders; removing a clean managed worktree through the GUI waits for an active turn, while the task repository API removes it from context immediately and defers clean worktree deletion until the turn releases; a bridge service restart preserves the cleanup intent and a fresh request completes removal; if the active turn writes files before release, deferred cleanup preserves that worktree and its changes; a dirty worktree rejects removal and preserves its task record and files.

The task context menu offers deletion. Pending repository tasks delete without confirmation and preserve the source repository; confirmed deletion waits for an active conversation turn; clean started worktrees can be deleted; dirty started worktrees require confirmation, and canceling preserves the task and worktree. CLI delete-check derives and reports the confirmation requirement from saved task and worktree state without resuming the Codex thread; confirmed deletion removes the managed worktree. Deleting a task also removes its per-task preferences and any left by already-deleted tasks, while another task's preferences remain.

A real worktree-removal failure records the task title and task, thread, process, phase, and underlying error details, including bounded NSError user-info keys and values, without recording conversation text; the failed task and worktree remain available and deletion succeeds after the repository is restored.

The default parent can be read, changed, cleared, and an unavailable path is rejected; a fresh CLI read and repository discovery use the persisted parent. Dark and Light appearance choices persist, the removed PR conflict preference is absent from CLI/XPC and Settings, and appearance changes update the open Settings picker. Clearing the default parent does not change roots already saved on a task. Before any root is set, opening the Add repository picker from the empty state's + still leaves Set root folder able to bring its folder panel to the front, every time it is clicked.

The configured-root workspace repos list API returns top-level Git repositories while excluding nested repositories and symlink targets. The conversation picker shows those suggestions, filters by repository name or parent path, and reports no matches for non-repository folders.

The CLI reads and writes ordered last-selected repositories across fresh XPC connections; repository batches prepare managed worktrees in order, use task-title-derived branches and main/main merge settings, and set the active task roots to those worktrees. The selected source repository list remains saved and applies to subsequent tasks. Invalid repository paths are rejected without changing the saved preference. In the UI, a new conversation automatically attaches saved repositories in order while the picker stays closed and the composer remains focused. Opening the picker and choosing another suggestion adds it to the ordered context and saved selection for subsequent conversations. Each saved selection also feeds a newest-first recent repository history of up to twenty repositories that keeps repositories after they are removed from the selection; the task repository recent command lists those that still exist and are not attached to the task, and rejects an unknown task. In the UI, attached repositories appear as large chips carrying a remove badge and the header shows no suggestion chips; removing a repository through its badge makes the add-repository picker list it under Recent before anything is typed, clicking it adds it back to the task and saved selection, and typing a query replaces the recent list with the regular search suggestions.

Applying an ordered repository batch with a valid repository followed by an empty Git repository fails without mutation: the CLI reports invalid_argument and fresh reads show no repository attachments or workspace roots; New Task automatically applies saved repositories; an invalid batch shows an error, attaches neither repository, keeps roots empty, preserves the saved order, and leaves the picker closed by default.

The CLI creates an Untitled task with no roots, logs task.create.succeeded for its ID, verifies empty history, and deletes it cleanly. New Task logs start and completion events with the same attempt ID and created task ID, then opens one empty conversation with the repository picker closed, the composer focused, and no create sheet. With no selected repositories, the empty conversation prominently says no repository is selected and, in place of the send-a-message prompt, shows a standalone round + button with its explanation, Add repositories to the task's context, as separate text centered below it; the + opens the header's Add repository picker and keeps the typed draft; typing starts immediately and, with a configured repository root, the UI enables standalone Send. Adding folder-only context leaves history empty, and backing out deletes the pending task without confirmation.

A real directory at the task-store write-lock path makes CLI task creation fail with operation_failed and leaves no task persisted; the paired New Task button shows the save error and writes correlated start and failure diagnostics with the same attempt ID, error domain, and code.

Creating a repository task leaves its selected branch pending while the composer automatically saves an unsent prompt as it is typed; clearing the composer clears the stored draft, backing out needs no Save button, and reopening restores the draft without creating a branch or worktree. Blank drafts cannot be stored, and invalid status changes are rejected without mutation. If the title is renamed while delayed title generation is in flight, the late result is skipped, the renamed title persists, and diagnostics record the skip reason without prompt or title text. A prompt saved through the CLI without submitting is an unsent draft, so the composer shows it when the task is reopened. A send that fails before any turn starts, such as one into a folder that no longer exists, returns its prompt to the composer as the draft, clears the pending marker and leaves the task out of In Progress.

Composer text typed while the agent responds is autosaved as an unsent draft together with its attached image, without ending the turn's submitted prompt or changing its status, and malformed draft images fail validation without changing the draft. A follow-up queued from elsewhere and dispatched after the turn does not replace the draft, which stays saved after the turn ends and is restored to the composer with its image after navigating away and after an app restart. Text steered or queued from the composer leaves the saved draft and does not reappear after the turn, and sending the draft clears it, its images leaving once the turn starts. A submitted prompt whose turn never started returns to the composer with its images, together with the draft typed after it.

Shift+Enter inserts a newline at the caret without sending and Return submits; multiline drafts persist, expand to the editor limit, remain scrollable and editable across reopening, and submitted prompts persist in history. In the UI the transcript's scroller stays hidden while the pointer is over the composer, shows at a subdued opacity only while the transcript is hovered, and hides again when the pointer leaves. As content is typed in short increments through successive wrapped lines after a line break, the newest insertion remains inside the visible composer viewport while its internal document follows the caret without scrolling backward. Typed straight quotes, apostrophes, and double hyphens stay literal rather than being substituted. Blank drafts cannot be sent or stored. Sending requires a configured repository root, while a task with no selected repository can still be sent as standalone. If a submitted prompt has no Codex thread or active send reservation after restart, the task returns to Waiting Response, clears its pending marker, preserves the draft, and returns it to the composer. Sending to an Untitled auto-branch task derives its branch from the generated title or prompt fallback before preparing the worktree and starting the conversation; if it is concurrently renamed while title generation is pending, the custom title determines the auto branch. A standalone Untitled task starts and persists its provider thread while background title generation is still pending. Stop is enabled as soon as the message is sent, while the turn is still launching and not yet interruptible. Diagnostics correlate title generation with the task and thread while excluding prompt and title text. Queued follow-ups persist with task and thread identity, dispatch after a completed turn, and remain visible for explicit retry after interruption. During an active turn, Return queues a follow-up and queued rows offer Steer. The obsolete footer Queue and Steer buttons are absent.

Selecting text in assistant and user messages, including wrapped multiline selections, shows a divided pill above the selected lines, Comment on the left and Side chat on the right, which opens nothing until clicked; Side chat opens the side chat bubble at the selected lines, and Comment opens a comment popover whose field, with the placeholder "Add an optional comment…", adds what is typed as a comment on the selection with its arrow or Return, closes, and never sends it to a side chat. Added ranges render orange and persist after reopening. The composer shows the pending comment count. Structurally recognized comment context is hidden while similar ordinary text remains visible; comments are sent in insertion order with source ranges alongside ordinary composer text. Multiple comments can be added before one send, comment-only sends are enabled, and closing the popover with Escape leaves none to submit. Pending comments take precedence over Goal-entry mode: submission sends them to the conversation, exits Goal-entry mode, and does not store the comment payload as a Goal objective. The agent is instructed to start each comment response line with the provider-neutral indexed protocol marker; the transcript renders that marker as a numbered prefix (1., 2.) whose hover opens a medium-sized hint with highlighted text and the user's comment, truncating long values while keeping them identifiable. The serialized payload and ordered response survive CLI/XPC history reload. Legacy Codex markers, response-annotations payloads, and annotation fields still restore their reply details. Consecutive paragraphs, headings, and list items of a reply form one selectable text: the comment reply's lines share one text with a paragraph each, and selecting across them adds one comment that highlights every covered paragraph, records the block it ends in alongside its start block and offsets (a comment inside one block keeps the original source fields), and is restored after reopening the conversation; the cross-block source survives CLI/XPC history reload. User messages render in a neutral gray, input-style bubble with a thin light border and light text rather than the blue accent fill.

Selecting text in a Claude task's reply shows a divided Comment and Side chat pill centered above the selection, and no bubble opens until its Side chat is clicked; clicking it hides the pill and opens a side chat bubble above the selection that starts compact and grows to wrap its conversation, wider once it has messages and taller with each exchange, until the chat reaches its maximum height and scrolls, keeping its text clear of the scroller. The bubble shows its messages in 14-point text, the selected text and a compact chat with no subtitle, whose composer has the conversation's model picker and a send button but no Comment button, Skills button or Plan and Goal buttons. Choosing another model and effort in the bubble applies to the side chat's next messages only: the task keeps its own model. The first side chat message forks the task's Claude session with --resume and --fork-session under a new session ID, read-only (Edit, MultiEdit, Write and NotebookEdit disallowed), with side chat instructions that list the Playhouse CLI and forbid reporting the task's progress or outcome, and the selected text quoted in the prompt; its answer streams and shows the source session's context in the bubble. A follow-up resumes the forked session without forking again, with the model and effort chosen for it. Asking it to create a task lets only the Playhouse CLI's board commands run, checked by a PreToolUse hook Playhouse passes in the launch settings (ahead of the user's own allow rules) and by its permission handler: a Write, an ordinary shell command, the CLI chained with & to another command and the CLI's task prompt with the options that would start a task are denied, while the CLI's task create, whose quoted description contains shell punctuation, really creates the task, and no file is written. The task's own conversation, Claude session, status and history are unchanged by the side chat. A side chat needs a conversation to fork, a selection, a non-empty message and a valid model and effort; an unknown side chat rejects follow-ups, and closing the bubble with Escape ends its live session without adding a comment, while the saved side chat's next follow-up continues the same forked session.

The first side chat message on a Codex task's selected text forks the task's Codex thread with thread/fork into Codex's read-only sandbox (excluding turns from the response, with approvals off and the side chat developer instructions), and every side chat turn names a read-only sandbox policy with network access, so the Playhouse CLI still reaches the bridge daemon. The answer streams, names the forked source thread and quotes the selected text; a follow-up continues the same forked thread with the model and effort chosen for it, reloading the fork in the read-only sandbox when the model changes, and asking it to create a task really creates one through the CLI, run inside the read-only sandbox, where the daemon accepts only board requests from a sandboxed caller, so the same side chat's task delete is refused as forbidden and the task stays. The task's own conversation, Codex thread, status and history are unchanged. In the app the bubble opens on the selection from the pill's Side chat button, has no Comment button, shows the question and the answer below the selected text, and a follow-up adds a second exchange. Closing a side chat keeps it saved, and its next follow-up continues the same forked thread.

Unsent conversation comments are saved with the task draft. Through CLI/XPC, a saved comment list reports its count on a fresh read, malformed input is rejected with invalid_argument and leaves the saved comments unchanged, a later draft save keeps them, appending a list adds only comments not already saved (how a send that ends without delivering its comments returns them without overwriting newer ones), and an empty list clears them, as the composer chip's Discard comments badge does. Saving comments after a sent prompt leaves hasUnsentDraft false, so the sent prompt never returns to the composer as a draft. In the app, comments added to a conversation through the selection pill's Comment popover are saved as they are added and survive switching to another task and back and quitting and relaunching: the composer shows the pending comment count and the highlights are restored. Sending them delivers their source ranges, clears the saved comments, and reopening the task shows no pending comment and no duplicate. Once sent, a comment can no longer be edited (task comments edit reports not_found), and clicking its text reopens it read-only in the comment popover, whose field can still add a new comment there. The comment chip's X badge (Discard comments) discards every unsent comment at once: the chip and their highlights go, the sent comment stays, and pendingCommentCount is 0 on a fresh read.

Clicking commented or side-chatted conversation text, without selecting any, reopens what it holds: text with only a comment opens its comment popover, text with only a side chat opens its side chat bubble, and text with both shows the Comment and Side chat pill to choose between them. A side chat opened on a selection is saved on the task with its source range, selected text, provider conversation, model and every answered exchange; closing its bubble keeps it, its text renders purple while no comment covers it and orange once a comment does, and reopening it shows its history and continues the same forked conversation, so its next answer is saved after the earlier ones. A comment is added on side-chatted text by selecting it and choosing the pill's Comment. An unsent comment opens in the comment popover prefilled to edit, with a Save comment button that stays disabled until the text changes and a Discard comment button: saving changed text keeps the comment with the new text, Escape closes it unchanged, Discard deletes only that comment, leaving the side chat and its purple text, and saving it emptied deletes it. Through CLI/XPC, conversation side-chats lists the saved side chats, a side chat's source must name a message and a non-empty range, task comments edit changes an unsent comment's text, empty text deletes it (as Discard does) leaving the other comments, and an unknown comment is not_found. Edits and side chats survive a fresh read and relaunching the app.

A side chat keeps answering in the background after its bubble closes. Through CLI/XPC, a first side chat message whose answer the provider holds completes once released and is saved with its exchange; closing the side chat with side-chat-close while a held follow-up is still answering does not stop it, and another message meanwhile is rejected as still answering rather than starting a second turn: once released the follow-up's answer is returned, saved after the earlier exchange and listed by conversation side-chats, and a further follow-up continues the same forked session, leaving the task's own session alone. In the app, the selected text turns purple as soon as the first question is sent; closing the bubble with Escape before the answer arrives and clicking the text reopens it with the question and Thinking, which the answer replaces once it arrives; after closing it while a held follow-up answers, going back to the board and reopening the task, clicking the text shows the answer that arrived meanwhile, and a further follow-up continues the same saved side chat.

A Claude turn that fails after Claude Code created its session leaves that session in place, and the next turn resumes it instead of claiming the same session ID again. After a Claude turn and Playhouse restart, if Claude cannot find its native resumed session, the retried fresh session receives the prior visible conversation from Playhouse's persisted transcript together with the new prompt. Claude completes the turn, and fresh CLI/XPC history and the visible UI retain both turns. A normal Claude resume continues using the native session without receiving duplicate handoff context.

After a Codex turn and a provider restart, a normal Codex send resumes the saved thread without handoff context. If Codex then reports that it no longer has the thread, Playhouse starts a new Codex thread, saves its ID on the task, and sends the prior visible conversation from Playhouse's persisted transcript together with the new prompt; Codex completes the turn, the replacement is recorded in diagnostics, the next send continues on the new thread without handoff context, and fresh CLI/XPC history and the visible UI retain every turn.

A Codex standalone chat page keeps its own thread: after a provider restart, a send on the page resumes that thread without page context. If Codex then reports that it no longer has the page's thread, Playhouse starts a new Codex thread, saves it as the page's provider session, and sends only that page's turns from Playhouse's stored chat pages as context together with the new prompt, never an earlier page's turns or the new prompt itself; the replacement is recorded in diagnostics, the next send on the page continues on the new thread without context, and the page keeps every turn in fresh CLI/XPC reads and the visible chat.

An Untitled Claude task with a pending auto repository branch uses its selected provider to generate the title before worktree creation; the branch and title persist across fresh CLI/XPC reads and the visible task. If Claude title generation returns no title, the prompt becomes the title and branch fallback, and the conversation still starts in that worktree. A fresh `task title` request reproduces the generated title and provider (null when generation yields nothing), and `task reconcile` returns the settled task unchanged.

Claude turns for different conversations run at the same time instead of queueing on a shared turn slot. While one task's turn is held active, a second task's send starts in its own Claude process, runs its own tool, and completes with its own user and assistant messages before the held turn is released. Each turn's process uses its own task working directory, each conversation keeps only its own activity rows and measured durations, diagnostics record no queued-slot event and no prompt text, and the second conversation's answer is available while the first turn is still running. The held conversation first completes a turn with a tool call. Before the held turn reports anything, its mid-turn history has only its question after that turn, with no assistant message or activity of its own, and it shows only a Thinking row with a spinner in place of an empty Working for, despite the earlier turn's tool call; once the turn settles, opening its Worked for shows no Thinking row.

A failing Claude turn does not disturb a conversation running in parallel. While one task's turn is held and then fails, a second task's send from a separate process completes on its own session and reaches Waiting Response; the failing task keeps its user message in its conversation, where the open and reopened task show it, with an empty composer and no unsent draft, records no final answer, and its provider process exit is the only failure in diagnostics. The UI shows the parallel answer after reopening its task with fresh history. While the failing task's conversation is open and its turn held, the parallel turn starts, finishes and advances only its own revision: CLI/XPC runtime still reports the held session active and interruptible and the parallel session inactive, and the open conversation still offers an enabled Stop and never shows the parallel answer.

Stopping one Claude turn pauses only that conversation while a second Claude conversation runs in parallel. The parallel conversation answers and keeps its own activity rows and measured durations while the first turn is still thinking; the stopped task moves to Waiting Response with no failure reason, records no answer, and leaves the parallel task's Waiting Response result untouched. A fresh CLI/XPC read confirms both results.

Two concurrent sends for the same task are serialized across the app and CLI/XPC paths against the local Codex app-server fixture; the second waits for the first, both complete on the persisted thread, the task remains In Progress while a send is active, and successful turns without outcome calls finish in Waiting Response.

When a steer misses its active turn, CLI/XPC and UI accept it into the durable queue for its own turn; opening an empty task waits for the model-aware prompt and omits the generic Start a conversation heading; with no active turn, missed composer and queued-row steers start their own turns without blocking other steering and leave the queue; queued fallback survives process exit or app relaunch and is drained exactly once; a missed regular or queued-row steer arriving during targeted queue dispatch is drained afterward exactly once; a follow-up being delivered stays claimed as dispatching and leaves the visible queue while its own turn runs; a missed queued-row steer from the CLI returns to the waiting queue and shows its row again in the app before the targeted turn ends; a failed targeted turn remains needs-action and does not drain later messages; malformed steer images fail validation; CLI/XPC steering routes image data to a UI-owned active turn and appears in the conversation. Command-Return steers the active turn with attached text and images, then clears the accepted draft and image preview; if the active turn changes before delivery, it clears the draft and queues the complete message for its own turn; a steer the provider refuses for any other reason reports the provider's error, is not queued, and returns its text and image to the composer with no message left in the transcript. Plain Return queues a follow-up with its attached image, clears the preview, and marks the row with its image count; the queued image persists across reopening without returning to the composer, and malformed queued images fail validation. Its row Steer uses the active turn ID, delivers both text and image to the provider, appears in the transcript with its image, and removes the item only after acceptance. The obsolete footer Queue and Steer buttons are absent and the active response control is labeled Stop response. Follow-ups persist across reopening, expose per-row Steer, delete, and more actions, and a distinct after-turn follow-up dispatches once after a matching completion and is removed only after successful delivery; removing an unknown queue ID fails without changing the queue.

Backlog draft images persist through fresh CLI/XPC reads and reopening the conversation, with the preview restored; saving more than 8 draft images fails with invalid_argument and preserves the existing attachment. The composer's attach button, left of the Plan button, opens a file panel limited to images, and the chosen image appears in the composer preview and persists as a draft image until removed; a non-image file picked anyway (through Go to Folder) is refused with an image-only error and adds no draft image. The conversation composer also accepts pasted images, compresses large clipboard images to fit the 10 MB payload limit, sends PNG and JPEG data URLs through CLI/XPC and to Codex using the tagged image URL payload, stores those image URLs with the turn in Playhouse's transcript store, and keeps earlier images visible after a later text turn and history refresh. The provider-neutral conversation present-image API is included in agent instructions, validates and persists agent-produced PNG and JPEG files as assistant messages, and reopening the conversation renders each image visibly. Diagnostics record image MIME and encoded size without storing image payloads. Clicking a composer attachment, a user transcript attachment, or an agent-published assistant image opens the original image in a large viewer, which can be closed to return to the conversation; a published assistant image preserves the original file bytes.
Malformed image data is rejected with a visible composer error and an invalid_argument bridge response, without creating conversation history or advancing task status.

While a Claude Code turn is active in the app process, the agent's CLI/XPC image publication joins that active Claude transcript turn; after the provider finishes, history places the image before the later assistant answer, and reopening the conversation renders the exact published image. Codex records the same active-turn attribution in the shared store, covered by test_codex_agent_image_published_during_active_turn.

A Claude Code agent that has answered initialize and gone idle receives a user message carrying a screenshot larger than its input FIFO's buffer: the send completes with Claude's answer, the agent receives the whole image, the user message keeps that image when history is read over a fresh CLI/XPC connection and when the conversation is reopened, and a later text turn in the same conversation still completes. Claude Code's runtime, like the kqueue-reading fixture, is never woken by one oversized blocking write, so such a message must reach it without freezing the daemon. Codex agents talk over a socket and are not affected.

While a Codex turn is active, CLI/XPC image publication avoids requesting provider history; the assistant image is tied to that turn, is recorded in Playhouse's store when published, so it follows the turn's prompt and precedes the answer that arrives later and the next turn in ordered history, as for Claude, and remains visible after reopening the conversation.

While a Claude Code fixture turn started by another caller is still running, its commentary and tool activity raise the task's conversation revision in the daemon's runtime snapshot, a held turn with no visible output yet leaves that revision unchanged, and mid-turn history, read from Playhouse's own Claude transcript, already returns the prompt, the commentary, and the in-progress tool activity before any final answer. A conversation reopened after its send, and so no longer reading that turn's stream, shows the commentary and the running tool row while the turn is still held, then the final answer once it settles; the revision rises again when the turn ends.

While a Codex app-server fixture turn started by another caller is still running, its commentary and tool activity raise the task's conversation revision in the daemon's runtime snapshot, a held turn with no visible output yet leaves that revision unchanged, and mid-turn history, read from Playhouse's own transcript store while the turn holds, already returns the prompt, the commentary, and the in-progress tool activity before any final answer. A conversation reopened after its send, and so no longer reading that turn's stream, shows the commentary and the running tool row while the turn is still held, then the final answer once it settles; the revision rises again when the turn ends. With a non-default model selected, those mid-turn history reads never send thread/resume, since history comes from Playhouse's store.

While a Claude Code fixture reply streams in held stages below its question, mid-turn CLI/XPC history holds every streamed line before the newest, which Claude may still extend as its answer, once each and in order after the question, with no final line until the reply is released, and the settled turn ends with its final line after every streamed line. In the visible transcript, a reader at the bottom follows the reply: once it outgrows the viewport, the newest streamed line stays in view and the question scrolls away. Scrolling up stops following, so the next stage leaves the reader's position unchanged and its lines out of view; scrolling back to the bottom resumes following, so the next stage's newest line is in view while the turn is still running; reopening the conversation while that turn is still running opens it at that newest line instead of at the question and keeps following, so the next stage's newest line is in view while the turn is still running and the settled turn leaves its final line in view. A short follow-up with a tool call then becomes the newest turn, and the newest history page ends with its question, tool call, and answer after the streamed turn. Scrolled as far down as it goes, the transcript has no blank overscroll: while the held reply outgrows the viewport it ends at its newest line, and the settled reply, whose streamed lines fold into Worked for, and the short follow-up, both once it settles and after the settled conversation is reopened, keep the newest question pinned near the top. Following is shared transcript presentation, so one representative provider covers it.

A Claude Code fixture turn that writes commentary, runs shell commands (one failing) and an MCP call, then answers keeps each call in Playhouse's own transcript placed after the message written before it. Once a later turn starts, CLI/XPC history still returns the earlier turn's calls as timeline activities, apart from the latest turn's activities: each shell call carries its stated purpose, its exact command and the output it returned, the failing call reports failed, and the MCP call exposes neither its arguments nor its raw result. A history page returns only the calls placed on its own messages, so the newest page carries none of them and the page before it carries them all. While its turn is the latest, a call stays in Worked for and is not shown inline. Once a later turn starts, the visible conversation shows each earlier call inline between those messages, in order, as a row with the tool's name, its purpose, and IN and OUT blocks clipped until expanded; the MCP row has no IN or OUT block, the turn's answer renders a numbered list written right under a paragraph line as separate items whose inline code text is unchanged, and the rows are still there after reopening the task.

A Codex app-server fixture thread whose earlier turn reports commentary, command executions (one failing) and an MCP call between its messages keeps those items in their place in history: once a later turn starts, CLI/XPC history returns each earlier call as a timeline activity placed after the message the thread listed before it, with its working directory, exact command and aggregated output, the failing command reports failed, and the MCP call exposes neither its arguments nor its raw result. Commentary on either side of a call stays a separate message instead of merging across it. A history page returns only the calls placed on its own messages, so the newest page carries none of them and the page before it carries them all. While its turn is the latest, a call stays in Worked for and is not shown inline. Once a later turn starts, the visible conversation shows each earlier call inline between those messages, in order, as a row with the tool's name, its working directory, and IN and OUT blocks clipped until expanded; the MCP row has no IN or OUT block, the turn's answer renders a numbered list written right under a paragraph line as separate items whose inline code text is unchanged, and the rows are still there after reopening the task.

MCP and dynamic tool lifecycle updates coalesce by stable item ID into distinct visible conversation rows; each call reports its start and measured duration, and completed durations persist through history reload. While a tool call holds the sent turn active, the transcript never shows blank space: the submitted user message is in view, or, once the turn's activity has outgrown the viewport and the transcript follows it, the message sits above the latest live activity, which is in view. The latest active process, including a long command, appears outside Working for on one truncated line; older active processes remain inside, and completion moves it inside. The conversation header has no live activity line while responding. Working for renders open while the turn runs, so its progress is visible without a click and lists the in-flight calls instead of a Thinking row, and it is still open after leaving and reopening the task mid-turn; every in-flight call is readable from mid-turn history. A collapse the reader performs mid-turn is honored and survives the activity updates that follow, and the final answer closes the section back into a clean collapsed Worked for. The expanded Working for list shows each call's live or completed duration. In-progress, completed, and failed statuses, server/tool identity, and safe result summaries render without duplicate rows in the live turn and in history reloaded from Playhouse's store. Arguments and raw result text are never exposed.

contextCompaction item/started and item/completed coalesce into one concise timeline event; missing summaries ignore malformed opaque payload fields and never render their data, and the event survives a fresh history reload from Playhouse's transcript store with correct prompt/response ordering.

Reopening a 120-message conversation, whose turns Playhouse holds in its own store, immediately presents only the latest user question, pinned to the top of the viewport with its answer below, which is taller than the viewport and runs on past its bottom. Scrolling upward reveals earlier messages automatically, a few at a time, starting from a reader already at the top of the rendered messages; they are revealed while the reader is near the oldest rendered message and stop once the reader rests away from it, while the message the reader is on stays in place and chronological order is preserved. A conversation that was empty when it opened establishes no window: when its sent turn streams sixty replies, each stored as its own message in order, it keeps the newest 40 of those 61 messages rendered as they arrive. Reloading history in place reopens on that same latest turn, pinned the same way, and keeps upward paging working: scrolling on to the top reveals every message, reading the stored page as needed, and reaches the first messages. CLI/XPC history remains complete and ordered across fresh reads and across an in-place provider switch, and a paged read returns only the newest 80 messages with the count of the 40 before them, while paging backward returns those earlier messages in order.

In a 120-message conversation whose history has been revealed, the messages before the newest turn render lazily: once the reader is back at the latest turn, the oldest messages that scrolled far out of view are no longer kept as views, and they render again, in order, when the reader scrolls back to them. A message scrolled away and back by the same distance lands where it was. A command an earlier turn ran stays inline after the message it followed, with its whole output in fresh CLI/XPC history, and a call the reader expanded is still expanded when its row renders again. A message holding an open side chat keeps rendering while the reader scrolls far away, so its bubble and unsent draft are still there when the reader returns. Changing the transcript's width keeps the reader on the message they were reading, with the older messages above still in order.

A sent prompt followed by 120 stored messages, so that it lies outside the newest history page, never returns to the composer when the task is reopened: the composer is empty, the task keeps hasUnsentDraft false and its last sent prompt as the saved prompt, and the CLI newest page of 80 messages leaves out the earlier messages. Only the saved draft flag decides draft restoration, so the same task restores a real unsent draft after it is typed.

Claude turns are stored row by row in the SQLite conversation store: a user image is kept out of the message text payload, and recording a later turn writes only that turn's own rows without rewriting earlier turns. CLI/XPC history stays complete by default; with --limit it reads only the stored turns covering the newest messages and returns those messages plus the count of earlier ones, and --before pages backward to the first message, with pages that join into the complete ordered history, carry its activities, and fill in the image only on the page that holds its message; this still holds after another turn completes. A non-positive or non-numeric limit fails with invalid_argument, an unknown --before message fails with not_found, and an empty conversation returns an empty page. Reopening the conversation in the visible UI reads only the newest page and pins the latest turn, scrolling straight down from that pin keeps the latest question near the top and the latest answer below it with no blank overscroll, and scrolling up then reads the older page from the store ahead of the reader, while loaded messages still remain above the rendered ones, until the first turn and its image are shown, and a turn sent afterwards from the composer keeps the earlier pages loaded without reading them again. A Claude conversation that never chose a model resolves it from its stored turns, in CLI/XPC reads and in the reopened composer’s picker: the newest assistant message that names a model, not an older turn’s model or the provider-wide remembered selection.

During a parent turn, Working for renders open and active agents appear as individual named rows, each with an arrow that opens it, outside it, with available path/model/reasoning metadata and started-working wording; a mid-turn collapse the reader performs is honored. When the final answer arrives, all agent rows collapse inside Worked for alongside other Codex activity; expanding it reveals clickable agent rows. The UI fixture pauses after the final answer to verify this before turn completion while Stop response remains available. Completed, interrupted, and unknown states survive history reload and remain inspectable after reopening. The child thread opens as read-only through thread/read, thread/turns/list, and thread/items/list without editable controls or thread/resume, and diagnostics retain safe RPC outcomes while excluding conversation text, command output, and diffs. Multiple Codex message deltas and command-output deltas are summarized per item with counts and byte totals, flushed at turn completion, and excluded from individual notification records; lifecycle notifications remain individually logged, and diagnostics exclude conversation text, command output, and diffs. A fresh `conversation subagent-history` read returns the completed child's stored conversation content.

Selecting Plan mode keeps planning active across completed turns and reopening; follow-up instructions start another plan turn, and Start Implementing is hidden until a first message is sent and while the agent waits on answers to its questions, then stays enabled with an empty composer, switches to Code mode, and starts an implementation turn; subsequent composer messages remain Code turns. The plan renders automatically as Markdown with visible spacing, remains selectable and copyable as one complete text view, and CLI events and bridge history preserve the exact plan text and latest implementation handoff.
